description.value: A block-designed fMRI cue-comparison paradigm presenting aversive faces versus neutral shapes.

spans.text: pictures of angry and fearful faces

description.value: In face-comparison blocks, participants viewed three angry or fearful faces simultaneously—one target face above and two faces below—and indicated which lower face was identical to the target. Four 32-second face blocks alternated with shape blocks.

spans.text: In a block of facial expressions, three faces were shown simultaneously, one target face in the upper row and two faces in the lower row.

description.value: In form-comparison blocks, participants viewed three geometrical shapes simultaneously—one target shape above and two shapes below—and indicated which lower shape was identical to the target. Four 32-second shape blocks alternated with face blocks.

spans.text: The presentation of the geometrical shapes was shown in the same manner, varying three different shapes per block

Task presentation was performed using Presentation software (Neurobehavioral Systems, Inc., Albany, CA, USA) and the experimental paradigm was presented via magnetic resonance imaging video systems goggles (Resonance Technology, Inc., Los Angeles, California).
pictures of angry and fearful faces

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to indicate with their dominant right hand which of the two lower-row faces or shapes was identical to the target in the upper row.

spans.text: Subjects had to indicate via button press which of the two faces in the lower row was identical to the target face in the upper row.
